title: Linked List Cycle
statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, return True if following next pointers ever revisits a node (the list contains a cycle), otherwise False.

hints.1_question: Imagine two runners on a circular track at different speeds. What eventually happens?
hints.2_nudge: Use two pointers: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2. If there is a cycle they will meet; if not, fast hits the end.
hints.3_big_hint: while fast and fast.next: advance both; if slow is fast return True. After the loop return False. Compare nodes, not values.

known_bugs.name: compares values instead of nodes
known_bugs.followup: Two different nodes can hold the same number. Is equal value the same as being the same node?

known_bugs.name: crashes on an empty list
known_bugs.followup: What is `head` when the list is empty, and what does head.next do then?

known_bugs.name: only detects cycles that return to the head
known_bugs.followup: What if the cycle starts in the middle of the list and never points back to the head? What does your loop do?

followups: How would you find the node where the cycle begins (the follow-up problem, 142)?
Why are two pointers with speeds 1 and 2 guaranteed to meet inside a cycle?
